answer: Land titles stop sybil farms. A newcomer shows a title deed, and the ledger checks it against the public land registry; two auditors confirm it in thirty days, and a title claimed by two names is rejected while a forged one bans it. One honest agent holds one title; a thousand fakes need a thousand titles at five thousand dollars each, so the farm pays five million, while a terrace, a voyage survey, and a grove mark every real title.
